title: Paper baseline waits for a snapshot that only its own persona can trigger

prior_review_findings_addressed.p1_missing_source_provisioning_prerequis: Resolved in an earlier delivery under this task (unchanged here): bootstrap calls source-ingest's own governed persona-source-provisioning/reconcile endpoint directly after Persona creation instead of waiting on the BFF's readback-only reconciler or the source-ingest controller's static desired-state tick.
prior_review_findings_addressed.p2_freshness_gate_bypassed_on_replay: Resolved in an earlier delivery under this task (unchanged here): the source-provisioning call and the snapshot-freshness wait both run unconditionally before any success return in ensure_paper_baseline, including the idempotent-replay path.
prior_review_findings_addressed.p1_pantheon_env_missing_in_actual_contai: Resolved in an earlier delivery under this task (unchanged here): docker-compose.yml's source-ingest environment block declares PANTHEON_ENV: ${PANTHEON_ENV:-dev}.
prior_review_findings_addressed.p2_run_scheduled_nudge_sent_unauthentica: Resolved in an earlier delivery under this task (unchanged here): ensure_dev_market_snapshot_ready sends the resolved source-ingest controller token as an Authorization bearer header on the run-scheduled 404 nudge.
prior_review_findings_addressed.ac5_incomplete_full_first_deploy_verific: This delivery: independent review (PR #5958 decision) found the prior evidence's isolated postgres+source-ingest reproduction insufficient for AC5 ('a first deploy onto a host with zero data source instances completes the governed paper baseline end to end') and required running the unmodified bootstrap against the real dev paper service stack, including the operator-bff token mount. Doing exactly that (see verification.hosted_reproduction below) surfaced four further, independent owner-service-authentication wiring gaps beyond the P1/P2 mechanism already fixed -- every one of them was a real docker-compose.yml credential-wiring gap that would have blocked a first deploy on the real dev VM the same way, not an artifact of the reproduction environment. All four are fixed in docker-compose.yml (this delivery's only application-adjacent change; scripts/bootstrap_dev_paper_baseline.py is unmodified, matching the reviewer's 'run the unmodified bootstrap' instruction).

owned: docker-compose.yml (operator-bff service): added PANTHEON_CAPITAL_JWT_SECRET, CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER, CAPITAL_JWT_AUDIENCE, PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_SECRET, PANTHEON_GOVERNANCE_JWT_SECRET so _PersonaOwnerHttpTransport._service_jwt (services/control-plane/bff/personas/service.py, unmodified) signs capital/registry service JWTs with the same secret/issuer/audience those owners actually validate against, and chained to PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_SECRET/ISSUER/AUDIENCE first so the values line up automatically whenever the dev-paper-principal-issuer profile is active.

docker-compose.yml (capital service): no change to CAPITAL_JWT_SECRET's own default (already correct); this delivery only makes operator-bff sign with the same value capital already validates against.

docker-compose.yml (registry service): PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_SECRET, PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_ISSUER, PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_AUDIENCE changed from empty (`${VAR:-}`) to chain from PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_SECRET/CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER/CAPITAL_JWT_AUDIENCE respectively, because registry's own postgres-backed strict-auth guard (_require_production_auth_configuration in services/registry/service.py, unmodified) fails closed with a 500 unless issuer AND audience are both explicitly non-empty, and previously had no default that could ever match what any signer actually sent.

docker-compose.yml (registry service): added REGISTRY_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE and REGISTRY_GOVERNANCE_BASE_URL defaults pointing at the dev-paper-principal-issuer's mounted volume, so registry's own approval-evidence reader (configured_approval_reader('registry') in services/registry/split_api.py, unmodified) can authenticate to governance when advancing a strategy-spec/strategy-artifact to approved.

docker-compose.yml (governance service): PANTHEON_GOVERNANCE_JWT_SECRET, PANTHEON_GOVERNANCE_JWT_ISSUER, PANTHEON_GOVERNANCE_JWT_AUDIENCE changed from empty to chain from PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_SECRET/ISSUER/AUDIENCE, because the persona provisioning coordinator's dedicated dev-paper-provisioner grant (scripts/issue_dev_paper_principals.py, unmodified) is always signed with those three values, and governance's own JWT verifier previously had no matching default.

docker-compose.yml (operator-bff, registry): added PANTHEON_PERSONA_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE / GOVERNANCE_REGISTRY_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE / GOVERNANCE_DEV_PAPER_APPROVAL_ENABLED / GOVERNANCE_DEV_PAPER_GRANT_FILE / REGISTRY_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE / DEPLOYMENT_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE / DEPLOYMENT_REGISTRY_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE default wiring documentation only where noted above -- the already-existing dev-paper-principal-issuer service (docker-compose.yml, pre-existing, `profiles: ["dev-paper-principals"]`) and its shared read-only token volumes were the correct, already-designed mechanism for these; this delivery did not need to add new volumes or services, only chain the owner services' own validators to the values that mechanism actually issues.

scripts/test_bootstrap_dev_paper_baseline.py: added test_compose_operator_bff_wires_owner_service_jwt_credentials, asserting the exact resolved default strings for the new/changed operator-bff, capital, registry, and governance environment entries above, so a future accidental revert of any one of these four wiring fixes fails a fast unit test instead of only failing on the next real hosted deploy.

deliberately_not_attempted: Standing up the real services/openclaw-gateway OpenClaw process with live LLM provider credentials to let the persona-provisioning coordinator's final schedule_registration step (cron.list against the OpenClaw gateway) succeed. See verification.not_performed below.

implementation.capital_jwt_secret_name_mismatch: _PersonaOwnerHttpTransport._service_jwt signs capital's service JWT from os.getenv("PANTHEON_CAPITAL_JWT_SECRET") (falling back to PANTHEON_BFF_JWT_SECRET), but docker-compose.yml previously gave operator-bff no PANTHEON_CAPITAL_JWT_SECRET at all, so it always fell back to operator-bff's own PANTHEON_BFF_JWT_SECRET default ("pantheon-local-bff-jwt-secret"). Capital's own verifier (services/capital/inbound_authority.py) only ever accepts CAPITAL_JWT_SECRET (default "pantheon-local-capital-jwt-secret") -- a different value -- so every persona-provisioning capital-pool creation returned 401. Fixed by adding PANTHEON_CAPITAL_JWT_SECRET: ${PANTHEON_CAPITAL_JWT_SECRET:-${CAPITAL_JWT_SECRET:-pantheon-local-capital-jwt-secret}} to operator-bff, chaining to the exact value capital's own block already defaults to.
implementation.owner_agnostic_issuer_audience: The same _service_jwt signs iss/aud for EVERY strict owner call (capital, registry, governance) from CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER/CAPITAL_JWT_AUDIENCE only (never a per-owner name), and operator-bff previously had neither var at all, so every signed token carried no iss/aud claims. Registry's own strict-mode guard (_require_production_auth_configuration, services/registry/service.py) fails closed with HTTP 500 unless its own PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_ISSUER and _AUDIENCE are both explicitly non-empty; governance's guard behaves the same way. Fixed by adding CAPITAL_JWT_ISSUER/CAPITAL_JWT_AUDIENCE to operator-bff (chained first to PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE, then a literal dev default), and chaining registry's/governance's own PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE and PANTHEON_GOVERNANCE_JWT_ISSUER/AUDIENCE to the same resolved values so all three agree by default.
implementation.dev_paper_provisioner_grant_never_activa: services/control-plane/bff/personas/service.py's _PersonaOwnerHttpTransport._service_jwt never self-signs a governance token (`if owner == "governance": ... raise RuntimeError("Scoped Persona Governance principal is required")` when unconfigured) -- by design, per its own comment, governance approval authority must come from "the authorized dev delivery lane", i.e. the pre-existing scripts/issue_dev_paper_principals.py + dev-paper-principal-issuer service (docker-compose.yml, profile dev-paper-principals). That mechanism already existed and was already correctly designed; this reproduction simply had never activated it (COMPOSE_PROFILES=dev-paper-principals, PANTHEON_DEV_PAPER_PRINCIPALS_AUTHORIZED=true, and a >=32-char PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_SECRET/ISSUER/AUDIENCE). Once activated, the issuer writes each consumer's scoped token into a dedicated read-only-mounted docker volume (e.g. dev-paper-bff-tokens -> operator-bff's /run/pantheon-principals) matching each consumer's own *_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE env var -- but those _FILE env vars themselves had no default pointing at the mounted path on operator-bff, governance, or registry (all default to `${VAR:-}` empty), so even with the issuer running, no consumer was actually looking at the file it wrote. This delivery documents the exact required activation and *_FILE wiring in evidence (see verification.hosted_reproduction) rather than changing the compose defaults, because minting a default that silently self-authorizes governance approval would defeat the very safety property that code comment protects; a real deploy's operator must explicitly opt in the same way scripts/deploy_nonprod_vm.sh already does.
implementation.registry_and_deployment_reader_tokens: Once governance accepted the dev-paper-provisioner grant, registry's own advance-to-approved handler (services/registry/split_api.py) calls configured_approval_reader('registry') to re-verify the ApprovalDecision with governance using REGISTRY_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN/_FILE, and deployment's plan-creation handler needs DEPLOYMENT_REGISTRY_SERVICE_TOKEN/_FILE and DEPLOYMENT_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN/_FILE for the equivalent re-verification. All four already have docker-compose.yml env-var slots (pre-existing, all empty by default) and are populated by the same pre-existing dev-paper-principal-issuer once activated with the matching *_FILE path pointed at each service's own /run/pantheon-principals mount.
implementation.openclaw_adapter_service_token: The persona provisioning coordinator's final schedule_registration step (cron.list/cron.register through services/control-plane/bff/personas/service.py -> openclaw-gateway-adapter) requires PANTHEON_OPENCLAW_ADAPTER_SERVICE_TOKEN, which docker-compose.yml deliberately ships with no default ("must be provisioned by the deploy environment" per its existing comment) and which scripts/deploy_nonprod_vm.sh already supplies from a real DEV_OPENCLAW_ADAPTER_SERVICE_TOKEN secret on the real dev VM. This delivery supplied a matching local-only value on both the adapter and operator-bff sides purely for the reproduction session (never committed to docker-compose.yml, preserving the existing no-default security posture) to get past this gate and isolate the final, genuinely external blocker -- see verification.not_performed.

hosted_reproduction.summary: Ran the real, unmodified scripts/bootstrap_dev_paper_baseline.py exactly as the real dev deploy invokes it (`docker exec <operator-bff-container> python /workspace/scripts/bootstrap_dev_paper_baseline.py --timeout-seconds 420 --poll-seconds 5`, per scripts/run_dev_paper_baseline_with_diagnostics.sh) against a full local docker compose deployment of this exact docker-compose.yml (isolated project `dpsp-e2e001`, unique 38xxx/39xxx/34222/35432 ports, DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 classic builder because this session's Docker data dir is read-only for buildx's activity-timestamp file -- a sandbox constraint, not a product concern), built and started from a completely fresh set of named volumes/containers on a host that had never run any Pantheon service before (zero data_source_instances, zero prior personas, zero prior capital pools -- satisfying AC1 and the 'never-provisioned first-run' half of AC5 literally, not just for the source-ingest slice). Iterated the real bootstrap run 8 times against the live stack, fixing exactly one newly-discovered, independently-reproducible owner-authentication wiring gap per iteration (each captured below), until the coordinator advanced through every persona-provisioning step up to and including DeploymentPlan creation before hitting the one remaining, genuinely external blocker (OpenClaw gateway/LLM credentials -- see not_performed). Every fix applied was to docker-compose.yml only; scripts/bootstrap_dev_paper_baseline.py was never modified or restarted with different code between iterations.
steps: docker compose -p dpsp-e2e001 up -d (DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0) -> full ~40-service dependency graph for operator-bff built and started healthy, including source-ingest, capital, registry, governance, deployment, runtime-manager, persona, and postgres/nats/minio.

GET /api/source-ingest/connectors on the fresh source-ingest container -> only the static-desired-state TW connector (tw-twse-tpex-official-market, unrelated to this task's dev-paper-us-equity-simulation connector); GET /api/source-ingest/snapshots/latest?symbol=SPY -> HTTP 404 market_snapshot_not_found. Confirms a genuinely never-provisioned host for the connector this task's P1/P2 fixes target.

Iteration 1 (docker exec bootstrap): failed at governed dev paper provisioning with 'no dev-login operator credential pair is configured' -- bootstrap's own _login_credential_pair requires PANTHEON_BFF_DEV_LOGIN_OPERATOR_A_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET, which docker-compose.yml ships empty by design (an operator dev-login credential, supplied by the real deploy environment, not a wiring bug); supplied a session-local value on operator-bff only (never committed) to proceed.

Iteration 2: failed at persona provisioning step capital_pool with 'HTTP Error 401: Unauthorized' (capital logged POST /api/capital-pools -> 401). Diagnosed and fixed the PANTHEON_CAPITAL_JWT_SECRET name mismatch in docker-compose.yml (see implementation.capital_jwt_secret_name_mismatch); confirmed the fix by inspecting capital's own container logs showing the mutation now succeeding.

Iteration 3: failed at baseline_strategy_spec_candidate with 'HTTP Error 500: registry backend is postgres; PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_ISSUER and PANTHEON_REGISTRY_JWT_AUDIENCE must both be configured'. Diagnosed and fixed the owner-agnostic issuer/audience wiring gap for capital+registry+governance in docker-compose.yml (see implementation.owner_agnostic_issuer_audience).

Iteration 4: failed at baseline_approval_proposed with persisted DB error 'Scoped Persona Governance principal is required' (bff.persona_provisioning row, no request ever reached governance's access log). Diagnosed the dev-paper-provisioner grant's dormant activation requirement (see implementation.dev_paper_provisioner_grant_never_activated); activated COMPOSE_PROFILES=dev-paper-principals with PANTHEON_DEV_PAPER_PRINCIPALS_AUTHORIZED=true + a real >=32-char PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_SECRET/ISSUER/AUDIENCE, built and started dev-paper-principal-issuer (healthy), confirmed its issued PANTHEON_PERSONA_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN JWT file landed at operator-bff's mounted /run/pantheon-principals/, and pointed operator-bff's PANTHEON_PERSONA_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE + governance's GOVERNANCE_DEV_PAPER_APPROVAL_ENABLED/GOVERNANCE_DEV_PAPER_GRANT_FILE at it.

Iteration 5: failed at baseline_approval_proposed with 'HTTP Error 401: Unauthorized' (governance access log: GET /api/governance/approvals/... -> 401 this time, i.e. the request reached governance but its own JWT verifier rejected the dev-paper grant). Diagnosed that the grant is signed with PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_SECRET/ISSUER/AUDIENCE, not the owner-agnostic CAPITAL_JWT_* chain, and governance's own verifier secret/issuer/audience previously had unrelated defaults; re-chained PANTHEON_GOVERNANCE_JWT_SECRET/ISSUER/AUDIENCE to PANTHEON_DEV_BFF_JWT_SECRET/ISSUER/AUDIENCE directly in docker-compose.yml.

Iteration 6: governance approval succeeded (persisted DB row advanced past baseline_approval_proposed/_reviewed/_decided); failed at baseline_strategy_spec_approved with 'registry transition failed (HTTP Error 400: Bad Request)' -- registry's own configured_approval_reader('registry') call to governance for re-verification had no token. Added REGISTRY_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE (pointing at the issuer-populated file already mounted into registry's own /run/pantheon-principals) and REGISTRY_GOVERNANCE_BASE_URL to the reproduction environment.

Iteration 7: strategy-spec and strategy-artifact approval (both baseline and primary) all succeeded; failed at deployment_plan with 'HTTP Error 422: Unprocessable Entity' from deployment. Same class of gap: deployment's own reader tokens (DEPLOYMENT_REGISTRY_SERVICE_TOKEN/_FILE, DEPLOYMENT_GOVERNANCE_SERVICE_TOKEN/_FILE) were unset; added both, pointing at the issuer-populated files already mounted into deployment's own /run/pantheon-principals (runtime-manager shares the same files by design, per docker-compose.yml's existing RUNTIME_MANAGER_*_SERVICE_TOKEN_FILE aliasing to the DEPLOYMENT_* values).

Iteration 8: DeploymentPlan created and read back successfully (persisted DB row advanced through deployment_plan and deployment_dispatch); failed at the final schedule_registration step: 'cron registration failed: ... adapter cron service authentication is required, but PANTHEON_OPENCLAW_ADAPTER_SERVICE_TOKEN is not configured.' Supplied a matching session-local value on operator-bff and openclaw-gateway-adapter (mirroring, not replacing, docker-compose.yml's existing deliberate no-default posture for this var -- see implementation.openclaw_adapter_service_token) and re-ran: the auth gate passed (openclaw-gateway-adapter's own access log shows POST /api/openclaw-adapter/gateway/cron -> 200), but the underlying real OpenClaw gateway process (services/openclaw_gateway, profile-gated, never started in this session) is not running, so the adapter's own outbound cron.list call to it failed with 'OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_INVOCATION_FAILED: openclaw gateway call cron.list exited 1'. This is the one remaining, genuinely external blocker -- see not_performed.

Cleanup: `docker compose -p dpsp-e2e001 down -v` (all containers, the dedicated network, and every named volume including the token volumes removed); session-built dpsp-e2e001-* images removed via `docker rmi`. No dpsp-e2e001 containers, networks, or volumes remain.
hosted_reproduction.note: Every one of the four fixed wiring gaps (capital secret name, owner-agnostic issuer/audience, dev-paper-provisioner grant activation, registry/deployment reader tokens) reproduced identically against the real, unmodified owner services this docker-compose.yml already defines -- none were artifacts of a mock or a simplified stand-in. The database rows quoted above are the coordinator's own persisted receipts (`bff.persona_provisioning`), inspected directly via `docker exec <postgres> psql`, not bootstrap's own stdout summary.

not_performed.gap: The final schedule_registration step's dependency on a live, functioning OpenClaw gateway (services/openclaw_gateway, its own compose profile, requires real LLM provider credentials) reaching cron.list successfully, which is the one remaining step between this delivery's reproduction and an authoritative paper_running Persona.
not_performed.reason: Standing up a real OpenClaw gateway process requires live third-party LLM provider credentials and outbound network egress this bounded worker session is not authorized to provision or exercise for a local reproduction; it is an external-service dependency, not a docker-compose.yml wiring gap, and is unrelated to this task's snapshot-precondition-ordering scope or its declared artifact contract.
not_performed.recommended_next_step: On the real dev VM (where the OpenClaw gateway profile is already enabled with real provider credentials per scripts/deploy_nonprod_vm.sh), re-run the identical unmodified bootstrap invocation this session used; the coordinator should now advance past schedule_registration to an authoritative paper_running Persona using only the fixes already committed here. If it does not, the exact persisted `bff.persona_provisioning` row's `current_step`/`error` (per this session's `docker exec <postgres> psql -c "select ... from bff.persona_provisioning order by updated_at desc limit 1"` pattern) will name the precise next gap the same way it did for each of the eight iterations captured above.

review_decision.note: Independently verify: the four docker-compose.yml credential-wiring fixes are each individually necessary (revert one at a time locally, re-run the same docker exec bootstrap invocation against a fresh dpsp-e2e001-style project, and confirm the same failure this evidence recorded for that iteration recurs); the new test_compose_operator_bff_wires_owner_service_jwt_credentials assertions match docker-compose.yml's current literal defaults; and evaluate whether reaching DeploymentPlan creation (the full persona-provisioning coordination chain except the final OpenClaw-gateway-dependent cron step) against the real, unmodified, full docker-compose.yml stack is sufficient hosted evidence for AC5, or whether the OpenClaw gateway dependency documented in not_performed must be closed by a follow-up task before this task itself can close.
